chunks: And it is narrated from Masʿadah ibn Ṣadaqah al-Rabaʿī, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said:

He was asked: “Why is the believer so severe?” He said: “Because the honor of the Qur’an is in his heart, and pure iman is in his breast, and he is a servant obedient to Allah and to His Messenger, affirming the truth.”

He was asked: “Then why is the believer sometimes the stingiest of people?” He said: “Because he earns sustenance from its halal source, and the pursuit of halal is precious and difficult. So he does not like any of his possessions to leave him because of what he knows of the preciousness of obtaining it. And if his soul is generous, he does not place it except in its proper place.”

He was asked: “Then why is the believer sometimes most inclined toward marriage?” He said: “To protect his private part from private parts not lawful for him, and so that his desire may not incline him this way or that way. So when he attains what is halal, he is content with it and becomes free of need from anything else.”
And he عليه السلام said: “Indeed, the strength of the believer is in his heart. Do you not see that you may find him weak in body, thin in frame, while he stands at night and fasts by day?”

key_terms.الرِّزْقَ: sustenance or provision earned by a person
key_terms.الْحَلَالِ: what is lawful and religiously permitted
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنِ: the believer, whose qualities are being described
key_terms.عِزَّ الْقُرْآنِ: the honor and dignity of the Qur’an residing in the heart
key_terms.قُوَّةَ الْمُؤْمِنِ: the believer’s true strength, rooted inwardly
key_terms.مَحْضَ الْإِيمَانِ: pure and unmixed iman within the breast
key_terms.يَقُومُ اللَّيْلَ: he stands in worship during the night

ai.seo_question: Why can a believer be strict, careful with wealth, desirous of marriage, and yet spiritually strong despite physical weakness?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the believer’s distinct traits arise from inner iman, reverence for the Qur’an, and obedience to Allah and His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. It describes caution with wealth, commitment to halal earning and spending, chastity through lawful marriage, and the reality that a believer’s true strength lies in the heart even if the body appears weak.
